import pandas as pd

def main():
    # File paths for source data
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/test_1.csv"
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/target_multisource_cot.csv"

    # Load Source 0
    # Schema: ['business_id', 'Score', 'date', 'type']
    df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, dtype={
        'business_id': 'Int64',  # Use nullable integer dtype to handle NaNs if any
        'Score': 'float',
        'date': 'Int64',
        'type': 'string'
    })

    # Load Source 1
    # Schema: ['business_id', 'date', 'ViolationTypeID', 'risk_category', 'description']
    df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, dtype={
        'business_id': 'Int64',
        'date': 'Int64',
        'ViolationTypeID': 'Int64',
        'risk_category': 'string',
        'description': 'string'
    })

    # Data Cleaning / Preparation:
    # - Ensure no leading/trailing spaces in string columns
    df0['type'] = df0['type'].str.strip()
    df1['risk_category'] = df1['risk_category'].str.strip()
    df1['description'] = df1['description'].str.strip()

    # Join plan:
    # Join on business_id and date to combine the Score and type info from df0 with ViolationTypeID, risk_category, description from df1.
    # Because df0 has Score and type, df1 has ViolationTypeID, risk_category, description.
    # Some rows in df0 may have NaN Score, keep them as is.
    # Use inner join to keep only matching records on business_id and date.
    # If multiple matches exist, this will create multiple rows (which is expected).

    # Merge on ['business_id', 'date']
    merged = pd.merge(
        df0,
        df1,
        on=['business_id', 'date'],
        how='inner',
        validate='many_to_many'  # Because multiple matches possible on both sides
    )

    # Select and reorder columns to match target schema:
    # Target Schema: ['business_id': integer, 'Score': float, 'date': integer, 'type': string, 'ViolationTypeID': integer, 'risk_category': string, 'description': string]
    target_df = merged[['business_id', 'Score', 'date', 'type', 'ViolationTypeID', 'risk_category', 'description']]

    # Convert dtypes explicitly to match target schema:
    target_df = target_df.astype({
        'business_id': 'int64',
        'Score': 'float64',
        'date': 'int64',
        'type': 'string',
        'ViolationTypeID': 'int64',
        'risk_category': 'string',
        'description': 'string'
    })

    # Export to CSV without index
    target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
